verdict: The M168 bank-service DSE is numerically and mathematically sound for its explicitly narrow boundary. Independent decoding of all 437760000 FC2 payload bytes confirms little-bit C-order packing, bank=input_channel modulo 8, all 120 SHA/size/popcount identities, 143894510 events and the published K1/K4/K8 output-block-weighted ledgers. The per-token formula is both necessary and sufficient for already-formed independent bank queues. K4 is a reasonable provisional implementation knee, but the free compactor, 3072-bit/cycle weight delivery, exact accumulator path and downstream commit are still open. Therefore 3.875660x and 5.843700x remain source-service boundaries and are not RTL, physical, FC2, FFN, network or system speedups.

packing_and_bank_mapping.decode_a: numpy unpackbits with bitorder=little, reshaped as token by channel
packing_and_bank_mapping.decode_b: independent byte shift-and-mask for bit positions zero through seven
packing_and_bank_mapping.layout_reason: C-order makes channel the fastest dimension and every FC2 Cin is divisible by eight, so byte bit b is channel modulo eight b and has no cross-token tail

necessity: one read per bank per cycle forces C at least max_b(n_b)
at most K total events per cycle forces C at least ceil(sum_b(n_b)/K)
scheduling_equation.sufficiency: Starting from C empty cycles, assign each bank to its n_b least-loaded distinct cycles. The cycle loads remain balanced within one; because total events are at most C*K, no cycle exceeds K. Each bank appears at most once per cycle, so the lower bound is attained.
scheduling_equation.scope_caveat: This proves scheduling only after independent bank queues exist; it does not prove that bitmap discovery, queue fill, SRAM response or accumulation can sustain the recurrence.

recomputed_population.population_isolation: Only the SHA-pinned M51 ten-sample manifest and its 120 FC2 payload files were consumed; no M39 profile100 record or denominator was read.

cout_weighting.stage0: 46809056 events times 1 output block = 46809056 K1 output-block cycles
cout_weighting.stage1: 33053865 events times 2 output blocks = 66107730 K1 output-block cycles
cout_weighting.stage2: 53067276 events times 4 output blocks = 212269104 K1 output-block cycles
cout_weighting.stage3: 10964313 events times 8 output blocks = 87714504 K1 output-block cycles
cout_weighting.interpretation: The multiplication is correct if each selected source group is replayed over all Cout/96 output blocks; the future RTL must expose and verify that recurrence.

k4_vs_k8.decision: K4 is the right first RTL point because it captures 96.89 percent of ideal four-way service scaling, whereas K8 doubles payload for only 1.508x additional service reduction. This is a provisional bandwidth/adder-depth judgment, not a measured PPA or energy optimum.

bitmap_scan_sensitivity.purpose: Expose the cost hidden by the already-formed-bank-queue assumption; these serialized figures are sensitivities, not measured speedups.
bitmap_scan_sensitivity.required_trick: Hold each compacted up-to-four-source group and replay it over every output block before retiring it. Generate the next group in parallel and buffer at least one group, avoiding a full bitmap rescan per output block. Stage 0 has only one replay cycle and is the hardest compactor-throughput case.

omitted_costs: bitmap fetch, set-bit discovery, per-bank queue construction, group arbitration and token-boundary bubbles
eight physical weight-bank organizations, four selected 96-byte signed-INT8 row responses per cycle, address generation, response latency and cross-bank routing
four-term signed reduction per each of 96 lanes, Acc24 update, overflow/wrap/saturation policy and arbitrary response/backpressure alignment
accumulator initialization and output retirement for zero-event tokens
BN2 fold/requant, residual read-add-write and any output materialization or next-layer handoff
clocking, SRAM macros, placed routing, SAIF/PTPX energy and matched K1/K4 physical cost
complete FC1, both ATLIFs, BN1 dynamic statistics/prefold, FC2 and residual FFN cycle composition

minimal_m168_rtl_contract.scope: One H67 FC2 sparse binary-input kernel with parameter K=1 or K=4, one shared 96-output-lane pool and an explicit boundary to the M160 BN2/residual commit.
input_identity: Cin must be one of 384, 768, 1536 or 3072; Cout must be one of 96, 192, 384 or 768 with the frozen stage pairing
binary input amplitude is exactly numeric one, from M51 C-order little-bit payload semantics
bitmap beats, module/stage, token id and output-block count are authenticated; malformed extent or reordered beats set a sticky protocol fault
compactor_and_schedule: bank equals channel[2:0], bank row equals channel shifted right by three
each source group contains zero to four valid events from distinct banks, with no duplicate, drop or invented event
the group is held while output_block iterates from zero through Cout/96 minus one; only then are its events retired
a next-group buffer and bank-cursor scheduler must sustain the recurrence or expose every bubble in measured cycle counters
zero-event tokens still execute the architecturally required accumulator/BN2/residual commit path
weight_interface: eight logical single-row-read banks with explicit request valid/ready, bank, bank-row, output-block and tag
at K4 at most four banks are selected and exactly four times 96 signed-INT8 weight elements, 3072 bits, may return in one accepted response
response latency and backpressure are explicit; no combinational zero-latency or free multi-row SRAM assumption is allowed
arithmetic: each valid binary source contributes its signed-INT8 weight unchanged
up to four weights are sign-extended and reduced exactly before signed Acc24 update
rounding, saturation or modular wrap points are frozen; bind the M160 maximum FC2 sum-absolute bound and prove no unintended overflow
K1 and K4 must be bit-exact at every 96-lane raw accumulator retirement under identical source order semantics
BN2 affine/requant and residual commit must either be implemented and counted or remain an explicit forbidden boundary
protocol_and_sva: arbitrary stalls on bitmap input, weight request, weight response and output commit
stable payload while valid and not ready, tag/address conservation, one response per request and no retire before all sources

covers for zero token, one event, four different banks, more than four active banks, all events in one bank, full bitmap, every stage width, every output-block count, concurrent next-group generation and forced protocol attacks
verification_and_measurement: commercial VCS only for RTL admission, with directed plus randomized SVA and a Python exact-output oracle
run matched K1 and K4 on identical payloads and identical memory-latency/backpressure traces
report token-accept to final-output-retire cycles, compactor bubbles, bank conflict cycles, SRAM requests, utilization and zero-token fixed cost separately from the theoretical source-service ledger
run matched Synopsys DC after VCS; add SRAM macro, STA and PTPX before physical or energy claims
do not admit an FC2 or FFN ratio until BN2/residual and all fixed costs are composed on the same ten-sample population
minimal_m168_rtl_contract.claim_policy: The first RTL milestone may claim functional K4 equivalence and measured standalone kernel cycles only. The published 3.875660x remains a theoretical bank-service boundary until the full contract closes.

findings.title: The independent bank queues and compactor are currently free
findings.evidence: The exact formula begins after eight bank event queues exist. A serialized 64-bit bitmap scan costs 54720000 cycles once per token or 138240000 if repeated per output block; the corresponding matched serialized K1/K4 sensitivities are only 2.899849x and 2.251604x.
findings.required_fix: Implement channel-to-bank cursors and a K4 distinct-bank group compactor. Hold each group across all output blocks while forming the next group in parallel; include all scan/fill/drain bubbles in the cycle receipt.

findings.title: The required 3072-bit-per-cycle weight delivery is not implemented
findings.evidence: Each K4 issue requires four independent 96-byte signed-INT8 rows. The DSE assumes one read per selected bank but contains no macro organization, request/response latency, address schedule or routed muxing.
findings.required_fix: Build an explicit eight-bank request/response wrapper with four selectable banks, output-block-qualified addresses, latency/backpressure tags and matched macro assumptions.

findings.title: K4 has no exact accumulator or numerical equivalence evidence
findings.evidence: Four signed-INT8 terms per lane, their reduction, the signed24 accumulator and overflow/saturation semantics are all outside M168. Bank scheduling may reorder channels, which is safe only under a proved arithmetic contract.
findings.required_fix: Implement the 96-lane four-term reduction and Acc24 update, freeze arithmetic order and overflow semantics, and pass a K1-versus-K4 exact-output miter under arbitrary stalls.

findings.title: The ledger is not a complete FC2 or FFN latency
findings.evidence: Zero-event tokens contribute zero source-service cycles even though accumulator retirement, BN2 offset/fold and residual commit remain architecturally observable. FC1, BN1, both ATLIFs and the full FFN boundary are also absent.
findings.required_fix: Compose bitmap/weight/accumulator fixed cost with the M160 BN2/residual path on the same ten samples before naming any FC2 or FFN speedup.

findings.title: Cout/96 weighting assumes a specific source-group replay architecture
findings.evidence: Multiplying each token's group count by output blocks is arithmetically correct, but the RTL must hold source descriptors while output blocks advance or else pay event-list storage or repeated scanning.
findings.required_fix: Make group-held output-block replay part of the state-machine contract and authenticate the block index on every weight response.

findings.title: K4 is not yet a measured Pareto point
findings.evidence: The selection uses payload width and reduction depth only. K4-to-K8 saves source cycles by 1.507795x while doubling nominal bandwidth, but neither point has area, timing or energy evidence and K3/K5-K7 were not explored.
findings.required_fix: After K1/K4 RTL, use a lightweight parameterized synthesis/cycle DSE for K2/K3/K4 and optionally K8 before freezing the paper point.

findings.title: No commercial RTL or synthesis evidence exists for M168
findings.evidence: The contract correctly records rtl=false, vcs=false and dc=false.
findings.required_fix: Close exact-SHA VCS/SVA first, then matched K1/K4 Synopsys DC; preserve logic-only wording until macro-aware timing and power exist.

findings.title: Backpressure and memory response bubbles can invalidate the ideal recurrence
findings.evidence: The equation schedules abstract events but has no bounded event-group FIFO, weight response queue, accumulator ownership or output stall model.
findings.required_fix: Exercise independent random stalls on every channel, prove no loss/reorder and report achieved issue/retire utilization versus the mathematical bound.

findings.title: The ten-sample result has no cross-sequence generalization gate
findings.evidence: All identities are exact but the population contains ten M51 samples only. The narrow result must not inherit profile100 or dataset-wide language.
findings.required_fix: Retain the ten-sample qualifier and later replay stratified sequences/event densities through the same exact cycle simulator.

findings.title: Bank-pressure distributions are not published
findings.evidence: The aggregate cycles are exact, but distributions of max-bank count, selected group occupancy and conflict loss are absent.
findings.required_fix: Emit per-stage group occupancy and bank-conflict histograms to guide queue depth, arbiter and clock-gating choices.

findings.title: Only power-of-two K values were sampled
findings.evidence: K1/K2/K4/K8 establish useful boundaries but cannot prove K4 is the exact cost/performance knee.
findings.required_fix: Add K3 and optionally K5-K7 to the software DSE when the RTL resource model is available.

findings.title: The production artifact states schedulability but does not emit a witness
findings.evidence: The formula is correct; the independent review supplied a constructive proof and 34708 constructor runs, but the production result contains only the equation.
findings.required_fix: Optionally add a small deterministic scheduler witness test to the next contract without changing the frozen M168 r1 evidence.

admitted: exact bank-feasible source-service cycles and Cout/96-weighted boundaries under already-formed independent queues
K4 as a provisional first RTL point
forbidden: calling 3.875660x or 5.843700x an RTL, physical, FC2, FFN, network or system speedup
assuming bitmap compaction, 3072-bit SRAM delivery, Acc24, BN2 or residual commit are free
mixing M51 ten-sample numerators or denominators with M39 profile100
PPA, energy, FPS, DATE headline or best-paper claim
